tut.c1.b: Quick views pull out running, protected, empty, old, and large sessions — plus orphaned data whose transcript is gone. Below them, narrow down by where a session ran or which project it belongs to; right-click a project to exclude its folder.
tut.c2.b: Every session this agent left on disk. Click to select, ⌘/Ctrl- or Shift-click for several, right-click for more actions, double-click to reveal the files. Click a column header to sort.
tut.c3.b: The selected session up close: resume it in a terminal, lock it so nothing deletes it, and see exactly which files a delete would remove. The panel button at the top right hides it.
tut.c4.b: Filter by title, project, source, session ID, or the first prompt. ⌘/Ctrl+F jumps here from anywhere.
tut.c5.b: Clear out orphaned data, empty sessions, or sessions unused for a while in one go. Running and protected sessions are always skipped.
tut.c6.b: Deletes the selected sessions along with their checkpoints and prompt history. Send them to the Trash to keep them restorable, or delete permanently. Delete/Backspace works too.
tut.c7.b: Sessions in excluded folders are never deleted. Set how many days counts as old, how many MB as large, and whether excluded sessions stay listed. That's the tour — the ? button replays it anytime.

tut.s1.b: Each agent — Claude, Codex, and more — is tracked in its own tab. The number badge is unread notifications; the pin sets which tab opens first. Pick which agents get a tab via the + button or settings.
tut.s2.b: The same 5-hour and weekly utilization as the /usage command. Yellow means over 70%, red pulsing means over 90%.
tut.s3.b: Today and last-7-days tokens aggregated from your local transcripts, with per-model chips. The chart button opens hourly/daily/monthly graphs.
tut.s4.b: Sessions running right now. Click a row to jump to that session's window; the folder chip opens the project folder. Right-click a row to hide it.
tut.s5.b: History of finished work and input requests. The orange dot marks unread — click a row or use 'Read all'. Clicking a row jumps to the window that session ran in.
tut.s6.b: The list button opens a window with every saved session — resume one, or clean out old and empty ones. The expand button grows the window for long lists; once expanded, a search button appears to filter by title, content, or project.
tut.s7.b: Each press of the bell cycles On → Alerts only → Quiet → Silent, controlling OS notifications and unread badges. Also available in settings.
tut.s8.b: Current version and the update check. When a new release exists you can apply it right here. The restart button relaunches the daemon; the GitHub button opens the repo. Reopen this tour anytime with the ? button above.
